event.summary: Keep the vendored-xterm hyperlink-tag contract test
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513.

TLDR: Existing sessions that still use the old terminal lose the regression check that their wrapped hyperlink warning reads the real destination correctly. A future vendored-library change can silently remove that warning coverage.

Details: This commit deletes the seven-layout test beginning at parent e2e/tests/terminal-links.spec.ts:1082 (deletion anchored at resulting line 1075). It was the test asserting real vendored-xterm getCell(...).extended.urlId values and shared tags across Claude-style reopened ids, Codex cursor continuations and wraps. SPEC_impl.md:1911-1914 explicitly requires it: "The field can change at a manual xterm upgrade; a browser test against the vendored bundle pins its presence and shared tag for both agent layouts. Losing it falls back to today's row comparison, never a quieter partial-match rule." Old terminals remain supported, per SPEC.md:3014 onward and SPEC_impl.md:1958-1966. The replacement grid test at e2e/grid-client/grid-attach.spec.ts:1247-1277 supplies pre-tagged grid rows via showScreen and cannot read the vendored-xterm field. crates/farhelm-ui/js-tests/terminal-links.test.js:477-496 constructs synthetic cells with the field itself; its adapter tests at 511-541 cannot catch a change in the actual bundle either. Targeted pinned-tree searches for urlId/extended.urlId/xtermLines and tagged-row checks found no retained real-bundle tag test. Preserve this test by mounting the existing static old-terminal harness and feeding OSC output there; creating tmux terminals on a current supervisor is unnecessary.

Suggested bucket: other (regression-test/spec-contract loss in maintainer tooling). Confidence: confirmed by source and contract analysis only; no execution or reproduction. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none (forbidden coverage metadata not read). Could-be-highest: no; no current security regression is established, and the existing fallback remains explicitly specified. Caveat: new terminal tag/mismatch behavior retains separate grid and pure-function tests; this finding concerns only the dependency contract of retained old-terminal support, not all wrapped-link coverage.

event.summary: Preserve production overlay disclosure regression coverage
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 647f0227b7f5b6c5fe443b2d5f0c4a20de0d5513.

TLDR: Removing this entire browser test file loses the checks that real approval cards, tunnel notices and quick-launch surfaces keep link destinations protected and refusal explanations readable. The remaining synthetic-cover tests cannot detect a missing marker or a wrong layer on the actual interface.

Details: Assigned patch 00831-001.patch:1-694 removes real-surface overlap/refusal tests, the launch-pill and overflowing-suggestions tests, both Delete-confirmation opening orders, and the final test enumerating every visible marked cover's layer. These guarantees remain shared by new terminals, not only the retired xterm test fixture: SPEC_impl.md:1973-1976 says links, hover checks, downloads and tunnels are shared, and its Session-host file reads section at 4060-4074 says "every surface that draws at or above the hover's layer and can overlap it carries a `data-link-cover` marker in its own markup" and "a browser test checks the explanation's layer against every marked surface it can render." Surviving tests e2e/grid-client/grid-attach.spec.ts:1408-1434 and 1763-1805 inject their own div with both marker and z-index:45. They establish the common gate but cannot fail if production launch_sequence.rs:752/774, approvals.rs:229 or tunnels.rs:466 loses its marker, or app.css:1793-1801 no longer raises refusals and lowers them beneath a real destructive confirmation. The static harness page at grid-attach.spec.ts:151-188 contains neither the production overlay components nor header confirmation layout. Pinned-tree searches for data-link-cover, disclosure-refusal, cover/refusal and confirmation/refusal assertions found no remaining real-overlay browser checks. Port the geometry/layer assertions to grid helper input in the real-stack browser suite before removing the xterm-driven versions.

Suggested bucket: other; confidence: confirmed regression-coverage loss by source/contract analysis, no runtime execution. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none (excluded coverage sources not read). Could-be-highest: no established current security or data-loss route from the deletion alone; the existing production markers/layers appear present. Caveats: common admission behavior retains synthetic browser and JS tests; this is missing production wiring and paint-order coverage, not a claim that current links bypass admission or that current warnings are hidden.
